title: Cap. III Sol. Rat. 8: mercy over all works — special mercy; few freed more illustrious
pass_a_gloss: Finally, what is urged, that his mercy is over all his works, does not make to the point. For first, God can exhibit mercy to every human being (which in truth he does) and yet not this special and outstanding mercy, that he adopt him as heir of eternal life. Second, the greatness of the divine mercy is not to be weighed from the multitude of individuals to whom it is imparted, but from the greatness of the benefits which are imparted to human beings, and from the unworthiness of those to whom they are imparted. For that God from his enemies, most contaminated with the stain of sin, and most worthy of eternal death, through the death of his most beloved Son, has willed to free however few, and to destine them to the heavenly kingdom, is a more illustrious specimen of mercy than that of justice, that he leave the whole wicked world to deserved destruction.
pass_b_english: Finally, the press that his mercy is over all his works misses the point. First, God can show mercy to every person (and he does) without that special, outstanding mercy of adopting them as heir of eternal life. Second, the greatness of divine mercy is not weighed by how many individuals receive it, but by the greatness of the benefits given and the unworthiness of those who receive them. That God from his enemies — most stained with sin and most worthy of eternal death — through the death of his most beloved Son has willed to free even a few and destine them to the heavenly kingdom is a more illustrious specimen of mercy than the justice of leaving the whole wicked world to deserved ruin.
source_text: Ad extremum, quod urgetur, misericordiam ejus esse super omnia opera ejus, ad rem non facit. Nam primo, potest Deus misericordiam exhibere omni homini (quod revera facit) et tamen non hanc specialem et eximiam misericordiam, ut illum adoptet in haeredem vitae aeternae. Secundo, magnitudo misericordiae Divinae non pensanda est ex multitudine individuorum quibus impertitur, sed ex magnitudine beneficiorum quae hominibus impertiuntur, et indignitate illorum quibus impertiuntur. Nam quod Deus ex inimicis suis, peccati labe contaminatissimis, et aeterna morte dignissimis, per mortem dilectissimi sui filii, quantumvis paucos voluerit liberare, et regno caelesti destinare, illustrius est specimen misericordiae, quam justitiae illud, quod totum mundum improbum relinquat merito exitio.
